title: Thermodynamics — Full Semantic Knowledge Graph
purpose: Semantics-first machine-readable representation of thermodynamics: concepts, definitions, laws, equations, variables, constraints, processes, systems, historical lineage, people, works, applications, limits and source traceability.

source_policy.preservation_rule: Source claims are preserved with provenance; normalized semantic relationships are explicit edges rather than silent substitutions.
source_policy.accuracy_note: The source contains pedagogical/simplified formulations. The graph preserves them as source claims while separating ontology semantics, allowing later refinement without deleting provenance.

core_semantic_distinctions.state_vs_process: States are described by state quantities; processes connect states and can involve path-dependent transfers.
core_semantic_distinctions.state_vs_path_quantity: Internal energy and entropy are represented as state functions; heat and work as transfer/process quantities.
core_semantic_distinctions.intensive_vs_extensive: Intensive quantities do not scale with system size; extensive quantities do.
core_semantic_distinctions.equilibrium_vs_nonequilibrium: Equilibrium has no macroscopic unbalanced driving forces/flows in the source's formulation; non-equilibrium systems require broader treatment.
core_semantic_distinctions.law_vs_definition: Laws are modeled separately from operational/mathematical definitions.
core_semantic_distinctions.potential_vs_property: Potentials are special state functions selected for particular constraint sets.
core_semantic_distinctions.classical_vs_statistical: Classical thermodynamics is macroscopic; statistical mechanics provides microscopic interpretation.

nodes.label: Thermodynamics
nodes.description: Branch of physics dealing with heat, work, temperature, and their relations to energy, entropy, and physical properties of matter and radiation.

nodes.label: Thermal physics
nodes.description: Broader domain encompassing thermodynamics and statistical mechanics.

nodes.label: Statistical mechanics
nodes.description: Microscopic/statistical description relating atomic or molecular behavior and quantum states to macroscopic thermodynamic properties.

nodes.label: Classical thermodynamics
nodes.description: Macroscopic, near-equilibrium description using measurable thermodynamic properties and the laws of thermodynamics.

nodes.label: Chemical thermodynamics
nodes.description: Study of energy relations in chemical reactions and physical changes of state, with emphasis on spontaneity.

nodes.label: Equilibrium thermodynamics
nodes.description: Study of matter and energy transfers between equilibrium states and calculation of final equilibrium states after specified operations.

nodes.label: Non-equilibrium thermodynamics
nodes.description: Thermodynamics of systems outside thermodynamic equilibrium; requires more general concepts and does not generally determine rates of approach to equilibrium.

nodes.label: Axiomatic thermodynamics
nodes.description: Mathematical discipline seeking rigorous axiomatic foundations for thermodynamics.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic system
nodes.description: Precisely defined region of the universe selected for study.

nodes.label: Surroundings
nodes.description: Everything outside the thermodynamic system.

nodes.label: System boundary
nodes.description: Real or notional boundary separating system from surroundings.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic wall
nodes.description: Boundary segment characterized by what it permits or prevents crossing.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic universe
nodes.description: System plus surroundings.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic state
nodes.description: Quantitative specification of a system under defined conditions.

nodes.label: State variable
nodes.description: Property determined by the state, independent of the path used to reach it.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic process
nodes.description: Energetic evolution from an initial state to a final state.

nodes.label: Process quantity
nodes.description: Quantity associated with a thermodynamic process rather than determined solely by the state.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic equilibrium
nodes.description: State in which macroscopic flows are zero and, for simple systems, intensive properties are homogeneous.

nodes.label: Thermal equilibrium
nodes.description: Mutual thermal balance used to define temperature operationally.

nodes.label: Mechanical equilibrium
nodes.description: Absence of unbalanced mechanical driving forces such as pressure differences.

nodes.label: Chemical equilibrium
nodes.description: Absence of net chemical driving tendency between phases/species under specified constraints.

nodes.label: Phase equilibrium
nodes.description: Equilibrium between phases under specified thermodynamic conditions.

nodes.label: Intensive property
nodes.description: Property that does not scale with system size.

nodes.label: Extensive property
nodes.description: Property that scales with system size.

nodes.label: Equation of state
nodes.description: Relation specifying constraints among thermodynamic state variables.

nodes.label: Constitutive relation
nodes.description: Material/system-specific relation connecting thermodynamic variables.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic constraint
nodes.description: Restriction imposed by walls, external conditions, conserved quantities, or other conditions.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic driving force
nodes.description: Unbalanced potential or gradient tending to drive a system toward another state.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic flow
nodes.description: Macroscopic transport of matter or energy.

nodes.label: Open system
nodes.description: Allows mass, work and heat transfer.

nodes.label: Closed system
nodes.description: Allows work and heat transfer but no mass transfer.

nodes.label: Thermally isolated system
nodes.description: No heat transfer; work may cross.

nodes.label: Mechanically isolated system
nodes.description: No work transfer; heat may cross.

nodes.label: Isolated system
nodes.description: No mass, heat or work transfer.

nodes.label: Temperature
nodes.description: Thermodynamic quantity associated with thermal equilibrium.

nodes.label: Pressure
nodes.description: Mechanical thermodynamic variable.

nodes.label: Volume
nodes.description: Geometric thermodynamic variable.

nodes.label: Internal energy
nodes.description: Energy property of a thermodynamic system; depends only on state.

nodes.label: Heat
nodes.description: Energy transferred by heating across a boundary.

nodes.label: Thermodynamic work
nodes.description: Energy transferred by work across a boundary.

nodes.label: Entropy
nodes.description: State quantity introduced by the second law and given an absolute reference by the third law.

nodes.label: Enthalpy
nodes.description: H = U + pV.

nodes.label: Helmholtz free energy
nodes.description: A = U − TS.

nodes.label: Gibbs free energy
nodes.description: G = U + pV − TS.

nodes.label: Grand potential / Landau potential
nodes.description: Ω = U − TS − Σ μᵢNᵢ.

nodes.label: Chemical potential
nodes.description: Material conjugate variable paired with particle number.

nodes.label: Particle number
nodes.description: Amount of a particle species.

nodes.label: Heat capacity
nodes.description: Thermal property developed historically by Joseph Black.

nodes.label: Latent heat
nodes.description: Energy associated with phase change.

nodes.label: Zeroth law of thermodynamics
nodes.description: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are also in thermal equilibrium with each other.

nodes.label: First law of thermodynamics
nodes.description: For a closed system using the source's sign convention, ΔU = Q − W.

nodes.label: Impossibility of perpetual motion of the first kind
ΔU = Q − W
nodes.description: Q is heat supplied to the system; W is work done by the system.

nodes.label: Second law of thermodynamics
nodes.description: Expresses thermodynamic irreversibility and introduces entropy; in the isolated-system formulation entropy increases toward equilibrium.

nodes.label: No spontaneous heat flow from colder to hotter body
Third law of thermodynamics
nodes.description: As temperature approaches absolute zero, entropy approaches a minimum; the source also states unattainability of absolute zero by any finite number of processes.

nodes.label: Adiabatic process
nodes.description: No heat transfer.

nodes.label: Isenthalpic process
nodes.description: Constant enthalpy.

nodes.label: Isentropic process
nodes.description: Reversible adiabatic process with constant entropy.

nodes.label: Isobaric process
nodes.description: Constant pressure.

nodes.label: Isochoric process
nodes.description: Constant volume.

nodes.label: Isothermal process
nodes.description: Constant temperature.

nodes.label: Steady-state process
nodes.description: Source description: no change in internal energy.

nodes.label: Reversible process
nodes.description: Idealized process whose intermediate states remain equilibrium states.

nodes.label: Quasi-static process
nodes.description: Process slow enough for intermediate states to be treated as equilibrium states.

nodes.label: Conjugate thermodynamic variables
nodes.description: Thermodynamic variable pairs analogous to generalized force and displacement; their differential/product structure represents energy transfer.

nodes.label: Fundamental thermodynamic relation
nodes.description: dU = T dS − p dV + Σ μᵢ dNᵢ.

nodes.label: Legendre transformation
nodes.description: Mathematical operation used to construct alternative thermodynamic potentials with different natural variables.
